messages.text: I’ll inspect the two benchmark files first, then trace the MCP server’s request, initialization, and file-update paths. I’ll keep this read-only and won’t build or run benchmarks.

The existing harness already has a persistent stdio MCP child with ID-matched responses, explicit initialization, and full JSON results. I’m narrowing the server-side trace now to establish which query tools it can exercise and how a changed source file becomes visible to a subsequent request.

The source freshness behavior has an important split: the benchmark launcher explicitly disables file watching, while production MCP watching is event-driven and only applies queued changes at a tool-call boundary. I’m checking the public update controls and their completion guarantees so the harness recommendation can distinguish “event likely arrived” from “snapshot definitely rebuilt.”

I’ve confirmed a deterministic freshness path: `refresh` is public and returns after synchronously replacing the analyzer snapshot; `update_paths` is implemented internally but excluded from the MCP tool allowlist. I’m handing back the transport, timing, and update guidance with the exact source references.
Investigation complete and handed back to the parent session. No files changed; no builds, tests, or benchmarks were run.
